{"id": "00000994-0000-4000-8000-000000000994", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "An Application Load Balancer (ALB) works at Layer 7 and routes on request content. A Network Load Balancer (NLB) works at Layer 4 and forwards connections with very low latency.

| | **ALB** | **NLB** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, TLS |
| **Routing** | Content-based: host, path, headers, query strings, HTTP method, source IP | Port and protocol only |
| **Performance** | Good, with some added latency from request inspection | Very high throughput, ultra-low latency, handles sudden traffic spikes |
| **IP addressing** | DNS name only. IPs can change. | One static IP per AZ, with optional Elastic IPs. It can also have a fixed private IP. |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions | Instances, IPs, and ALBs |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023, but optional) |
| **Built-in auth** | Supports OIDC and Amazon Cognito authentication | Not supported |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS, with SNI and multiple certificates | Terminates TLS, with SNI and multiple certificates, or passes it through to targets |
| **PrivateLink** | Not a direct endpoint service provider | Can front an endpoint service (AWS PrivateLink) |
| **Extras** | Redirects, fixed responses, weighted target groups, WAF integration | Preserves the client source IP, supports long-lived connections |

**Choose an ALB when:**
- You run HTTP/HTTPS web apps, microservices, or APIs.
- You need path-based or host-based routing, such as `/api` going to one service and `/web` to another.
- You want WAF, authentication offload, or Lambda targets.

**Choose an NLB when:**
- You need extreme performance or millions of requests per second with minimal latency.
- Your traffic is non-HTTP, such as TCP or UDP (gaming, IoT, DNS, custom protocols).
- You need static or Elastic IPs, for example so customers can allowlist them.
- You want to expose a service through PrivateLink.

You can also combine them. Putting an ALB behind an NLB gives you static IPs and PrivateLink support in front of Layer 7 routing.

I can look at the load balancers in your account if you'd like, for example to check which types you're running or how their targets are doing.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
